### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**6** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c9ef6538bf647d4ab7dabd0f04f5913193f88bc5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a741454f481f47f97626ffde431c42113413ae82` — the merge of head `a61501aaae21fdf9d20fad658a364a3a4a64385a` into base `c9ef6538bf647d4ab7dabd0f04f5913193f88bc5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a741454f481f47f97626ffde431c42113413ae82 && git checkout a741454f481f47f97626ffde431c42113413ae82
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin c9ef6538bf647d4ab7dabd0f04f5913193f88bc5 a61501aaae21fdf9d20fad658a364a3a4a64385a && git checkout -B drift-repro c9ef6538bf647d4ab7dabd0f04f5913193f88bc5 && git merge --no-ff a61501aaae21fdf9d20fad658a364a3a4a64385a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json c9ef6538bf647d4ab7dabd0f04f5913193f88bc5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT (L1, first read; landing waits on CI) · Head-sha: a61501aaae21fdf9d20fad658a364a3a4a64385a · 2026-11-16T17:49Z

L1 thread L1-a, routed by the seat for card #34206 (route C). I read the final-head comment 6924350511, dev report 6924328376, maintainer ruling 6920925378 (letter B: a metadata change signal plus a cache of caller-independent compiled results, and no per-caller bundle cache), route records 6919864431, 6919887033 and 6920972383, the PR body, and the full diff against merge base `9e6fee19`: 3 files, +185/−8. The PR is not governed, and no L2 is owed (`Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, no `packages/spec/src/**` file, no narrowing).

- **Card relation.** `Part of #34206`, which is right. This is C, the first of the three steps in claim amendment 2 (C, then the ADR PR, then the shared compile cache), and the card stays open.
- **Ruling fit.** The memo holds a caller-independent result (the closure reads no caller, row, context or option). It is keyed on the registry's existing `objectRevision`, which is the change signal the ruling names. There is no per-caller cache.
- **The memo** (`engine-references-and-master-detail.ts`).
  - It is a module `WeakMap` keyed on the facet host. `referencesAndMasterDetailHost.of(engine)` is itself a per-engine `WeakMap` (`engine-facet-hosts.ts`), so there is one memo per engine for the engine's life. `_registry` is never reassigned in source, so the memo cannot outlive the registry it was filled from.
  - The stamp is `objectRevision`. When it moves, the whole memo is replaced. A registry with no numeric counter computes on every call.
  - Only names the registry holds are remembered (`computed === undefined` returns early), so caller input cannot grow the memo.
  - The stored list is frozen, and every call returns `[...answer]`, a fresh array as before.
  - The uncached body (`computeCascadeDeleteObjects`) is the old body moved verbatim. `collectCascadeDeleteObjects`, `cascadeRelationBehavior` and the delete walk are untouched.
- **Is the key sound? Re-read on this head.**
  - *What the closure reads.* `cascadeRelationBehavior` (`engine-cascade-planning.ts:584`) reads the field definition (`statesDeleteSemantics`, `deleteWalkTargetOf`), `resolveObjectName`, and `isFederatedUnprovisionedInjectedColumn`. That last one is `isFederatedObject(schema) && resolveInjectedColumnProvenance(schema, field)`, a pure function of the definition. `getObject`, `resolveObjectName` and `getAllObjects` read the registry only.
  - *Where the merged-object cache is dropped.* Every drop of `mergedObjectCache` in source moves `_objectRevision`:
    - `registry-object-registration.ts:633/636`;
    - `invalidate`, `invalidateAll` and `reset` (`registry-picklists.ts:469/486/502`);
    - the four sites in `registry-platform-global.ts` (607/624/721/753).
  - *The one drop without its own bump.* `noteObjectEntry`'s restore closure (`registry-restore.ts:225`). It runs only from `point.restore()` in `restoringOnRefusal`'s catch, which calls `invalidateAll()` on the next line (`registry-restore.ts:96–98`). A nested run adopts its point into the outer one, so the outer catch restores and bumps.
  - So the memo is exactly as fresh as the registry's own merged-object cache, as the body claims.
- **Pins.** Seven, in a new `describe` in `engine-cascade-delete-objects.test.ts`:
  - a second call does no walk (a spy on `cascadeRelationBehavior`);
  - registering a cascading child moves the revision and is named;
  - unregistering one drops it;
  - a `view` registration that leaves the revision alone keeps the memo, with non-vacuity asserts that the view landed and the counter did not move;
  - cached equals uncached for every fixture object plus an unknown name, the uncached answer taken through a registry whose counter is hidden;
  - a fresh copy per call;
  - an unknown name answers `undefined` and is answered once registered.

  The existing protocol pin "an object registered later … is on the next read" also goes red under the never-invalidate ablation. All three ablations in the body went red and were restored.
- **Measured** (body): Setup bundle meta median from about 184 ms to about 147 ms, and about 464 ms to about 356 ms after a minute idle.
- **Changeset.** I checked each sentence against the diff: `patch` on `@objectstack/objectql`, "remembers its answer per object name until the schema registry's `objectRevision` moves", "every registry change that drops the registry's merged-object cache also moves `objectRevision`" (true by the sites above), and "each call still gets its own copy". Every one matches the code above.
- **Checks on this head** (check-runs when I read): 48 names, 12 success, 16 skipped, 20 still running (Test Core 1–8/8, Build Core, Live E2E UI, the Type Check and Lint jobs), and 0 failed. Landing needs them green. `check:platform-checklist`, the known red on main (stopgap #34435), is not this PR's.
- **Base.** PRBASE is `c9ef6538` (Test Core plan), and K = 0. `git merge-tree` against current main is clean.

### Notes (not blocking)

- **N1.** Package enable and disable reach the closure only through `invalidateAll`, and the refused-registration restore only through the `invalidateAll` after `point.restore()`. Both are correct by reading, but neither has a pin of its own: the invalidation pins cover register and unregister. A one-line pin each (disable a package that owns a cascading child, then the next answer drops it; a refused registration run, then the answer equals the one before it) would keep the "every drop moves the revision" claim honest if a later edit adds a drop site without a bump. These can ride the next PR of the series.
- **N2.** The memo docblock's limit ("a subclass or spy that changes `cascadeRelationBehavior`'s answer after the first call at a revision") is accurate and confined to tests. No change needed.

Landing: not Tier H, and no L2 owed. The seat lands it once its checks are green.
